quiz.prompt: Explain concurrency vs parallelism using the event loop and the GIL.
rubric: Concurrency = interleaving progress on many tasks
Parallelism = simultaneous execution on multiple cores
Event loop switches at await points (single thread)
GIL lets one thread run Python bytecode at a time; processes bypass it

capstone.title: Study tracker CLI v1
capstone.brief: (12h) Build from an empty file a typed CLI: argparse subcommands add/list/done/stats; dataclass models + Priority enum; JSON storage behind a Storage Protocol; regex-validated input; custom exceptions; zoneinfo-aware timestamps; generator-based CSV export; an async `quote` command (httpx, timeout); ≥15 pytest tests incl. failures and tmp files; mypy --strict clean. Log AI-assistant use. Can double as your CS50P Problem Set 9 final project. Pass ≥8/10 with no zero in the last row.

rubric.criterion: Correctness (all commands; empty file, bad input, timeout)
Code design (functions, dataclasses, Protocol, no globals, main guard)
Tests (≥15, cover errors and tmp files)
Explain & modify live (reviewer change in ≤20 min without AI)
